subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: monthly tokens + peak TPS
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-14T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: monthly tokens + peak TPS

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we can size cost and propose a hosted API plan that meets FintechX's needs:

What I captured on the call:
- Primary use case: real-time customer support assistant + transaction summarization (post-transaction notifications).
- Integration point: server-side calls from your support backend and batch summarization jobs overnight.
- Success metrics: <50ms latency target for chat paths, 99th pct SLA for peak traffic windows.

To move pricing forward, could you confirm two numbers so we can model unit economics:
1) Expected monthly token volume (best estimate range is fine — e.g., 0.5M / 5M / 50M tokens).
2) Peak TPS (tokens per second) during high traffic windows — this helps us size reserved capacity vs. burst.

As context, customers at your scale typically target cost bands in the $300-$1,200 per 1M tokens range depending on model and latency SLOs. If you have a target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for, share that too and we can propose batching/quantization options.

I'm attaching a quick usage_estimate_template.xlsx you can fill with sample traffic to make this easier. Once we have those numbers, Marissa and I will propose a Hosted API plan and upfront vs. committed pricing scenarios.

Next steps:
- Sophie: share monthly token range + peak TPS and any target $/1M tokens (or budget range).
- Redwood: send a short pricing model and recommended config (batching, cache, model tier) after numbers are in.

Thanks — talk soon.

Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachment: usage_estimate_template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@fintechx.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: monthly tokens + peak TPS

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the clear recap. Per our internal analytics team, here's the ballpark for now:

- Expected monthly token volume (approx): 8M-12M tokens/month (chat + background summarization).
- Peak TPS (tokens per second): we see spikes up to ~120 tokens/sec during morning support ramp; sustained peaks around 40-60 tps the rest of the day.
- Budget target: we'd like to land somewhere around $600-$900 per 1M tokens if possible.

I attached a quick snapshot from our traffic dashboard (prod_traffic_snapshot.png) that shows the typical hourly distribution. We can refine the monthly estimate after we export a 30-day token-level report — I can share that by end of week if helpful.

Let us know what config you recommend for hitting latency targets while staying in the target cost band. Also flag any minimum commit that affects price.

Best,
Sophie Chen
Head of Product
FintechX
sophie.chen@fintechx.com

Attachment: prod_traffic_snapshot.png (image stub)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-15T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing qualification: monthly tokens + peak TPS

Internal — quick note on strategy after Sophie's reply:

- Volume: 8-12M/mo and peak ~120 tps. Budget target $600-$900 per 1M tokens.
- Recommendation: propose Hosted API plan with optional committed tier at 6-9 months to hit the low end of target pricing. Include options:
  * No-commit hosted: higher unit price but zero lock-in.
  * Committed reservation: 20-30% discount for 6-12 month commit (model-dependent).
- Technical: Rachel, can you size whether a standard n1/gpu pool (or model variant) meets 120 tps peak with our low-latency kernel? If not, propose autoscale/burst config.

I'll draft the pricing model once Rachel confirms capacity sizing.

Alex

Sophie,

Appreciate the details, that gives us a good starting point. We'll do two things next:

1) Rachel will validate capacity for 120 tps and recommended autoscale/burst headroom. Expect a short note by EOD.
2) I'll send a simple pricing model with: no-commit hosted unit price, 6-month and 12-month committed options, and a runway scenario showing how batching/caching could push effective $/1M tokens toward your $600 target.

If you can share the 30-day token export later this week, we can swap the modeled numbers for actuals and tighten the proposal. Otherwise we'll model using 10M tokens/mo as the midpoint.

Proposed timeline:
- Wed: sizing note from Rachel
- Thu: pricing model + recommended config

Thanks — talk soon.
